body:
Redline round 1

Reviewed the whole pull request.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at 48c971b returned 21 candidates: 0 confirmed, 0 for the person, 9 collapsed into findings already reported or settled, 10 already tracked, 2 dropped (refuted, outside the diff or disproportionate).

This round reviewed the working tree at 474593f, not the 48c971b its prompt names, because the relaunch reran round 1's reviewer on the cached round 1 coverage candidates. At that head every one of the 21 candidates collapses into something already on the PR. Seven match R1-1 to R1-6, whose fixes are in the tree and no longer reproduce. Ten match the round 1 review's For the person list and still read as described there. Two collapse into those ten, and two remain disproportionate. Nothing new is confirmed. The Docs, Version and scheduled-work checks raise nothing: the plan names a docs section for every change, the version goes from main's 0.1.1 to 0.2.0, and this repository has no routes/console.php. The person should read the For the person entry first: this relaunch is not a replay of round 1, and a round 1 that confirms nothing new hands the PR off while R3-3 and R3-4 are still open.

No findings.

### For the person

- `workflows/redline-loop.js:1165` · This relaunch is not a replay of round 1. The plugin loads in place, and the round 1 reviewer prompt now carries the R2-1 reopen sentence, which was absent at 48c971b. So the reviewer reran at 474593f on the cached coverage r1 candidates, while the prompt still names 48c971b. The agents after it rerun as well. post r1 rewrites the untracked round-1-findings.json and round-1-review.json in the round 1 folder before has-review skips the post. A round 1 with no new finding then hands the PR off (line 3339) while R3-3 and R3-4 are still open. Neither the README's in-place Known limit nor agent-os/standards/workflow/replay.md says that a self-hosted relaunch stops replaying once a round changes prompt text.
